summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to discuss phases 42, 43, and 44 of the cipher-box project, extracting implementation decisions for three security/durability bugs so downstream plan agents can act without further user input.
summary.outcome: Phases 42 (api-unpin-integrity) and 43 (fuse-write-durability) were fully discussed and CONTEXT.md + DISCUSSION-LOG.md committed for each; Phase 44 discussion was started but the session was cut off mid-analysis before decisions were locked.

repo: The IPFS unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) is guarded only by JwtAuthGuard and never reads req.user — any valid JWT can unpin any CID, making cross-tenant data destruction a low-effort attack.

Kubo v0.40 runs with the 'server' profile (disables LAN discovery only) and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly, meaning every pinned CID is broadcast via DHT provider records — CIDs are effectively enumerable by crawlers even though blobs are encrypted.
Kubo API port 5001 is loopback-only since Phase 29 — the NestJS API endpoint is the sole external unpin path.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without calling unpin (shared-write.ts:450), so there is no cross-user legitimate unpin path today.
Web and FUSE callers silently swallow unpin errors: web uses .catch(logger.warn), FUSE uses 'let _ ='  — so a 403 response would produce warn-log noise without breaking anything currently.
BYO-IPFS injects a provider.unpin function but it is not wired into server-side delete flows; only advisory row removal happens for BYO users.
IPNS records are published to the public IPFS network for TEE republishing and recovery, giving anyone observing an IPNS name a way to resolve the current metadata CID.
The FUSE write path uses a queue (crates/sdk/src/queue.rs) for publish operations, but release() does not wait for the remote commit before returning success to the OS — the data-loss window.
FUSE mkdir creates parent directories whose IPNS publish can orphan if the process crashes mid-tree (fuse-mkdir-parent-publish-orphan bug).

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global Kubo pin/rm on a CID without ownership check — content-addressed dedup means this can destroy another user's pin.
Kubo v0.40 configured with 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed tcp+udp — full public DHT participation, so provider records for every pinned CID are publicly harvestable.
Web unpin caller ignores errors via .catch(logger.warn) — changing unpin response codes is safe from a breakage standpoint but will generate warn-log noise for benign races.
FUSE release() returns before the queued remote publish commits, creating a data-loss window if the process crashes between OS acknowledgment and IPFS pin.
SDK publish queue used by FUSE — the queue mechanics determine whether an outbox/WAL pattern for durability is feasible without redesigning the write path.
Phase 44 source file — being analyzed for quota-decrement-on-unpin bug when session ended; findings incomplete.

workflow: GSD discuss produces three artifacts per phase: CONTEXT.md (decisions for downstream agents), DISCUSSION-LOG.md (rationale trail), and DISCUSS-CHECKPOINT.json (structured decision state); all three are committed to git before the manager resumes.

The manager runs discuss inline (needs user interaction) and dispatches plan/execute as background agents — on Claude Code, plan and execute also run inline despite the background framing because nested Agent() calls don't work in backgrounded agents.
When the assistant answered a direct question with another option menu instead of a plain answer, the user explicitly corrected this — direct factual answers should precede any option presentation.

friction: Assistant presented an option menu in response to a direct factual question ('how would a caller unpin a CID they don't own?'), requiring explicit user correction before giving a straight answer.
Session hit a usage limit mid-Phase 44 discussion, forcing the user to re-submit the same message after the reset — Phase 44 had to restart from scratch.
Phase 42 git commit required a follow-up verification bash call because it was unclear whether the commit landed — an extra round-trip that broke flow.
